name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.ArithmeticStageBounds.powerBound_of_fifth
theorem_title: Fifth-power domination transfers an exponent bound
natural_language_statement:
Let $f,g:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N$ and $a\in\mathbb R$. If $g$ has power bound $a$ and $f(n)^5\le256g(n)^8$ for every $n$, then $f$ has power bound $8a/5$.

This estimate converts the fifth-power arithmetic comparison into the exponent bound used for convolution costs.
explanation: Take logarithms of the finite comparison and apply the given power bound. This estimate converts the fifth-power arithmetic comparison into the exponent bound used for convolution costs.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored.read
theorem_title: Reading a stored original-index incidence
natural_language_statement:
Let memory $\mu$ contain the parallel value, owner, and position arrays for the incidence list constructed from length $n$, band size $g$, records $R$, and original value map $f$. At every valid list index $k$, the three reads equal respectively $f$ at the labelled original position, its owner label, and its original position.

These reads let a physical wanted slot recover its original A value, owner label, and original input position.
explanation: Unpack the stored predicate at the chosen list index. These reads let a physical wanted slot recover its original A value, owner label, and original input position.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandRawA.row_stored
theorem_title: A band row satisfies the stored-incidence relation
natural_language_statement:
Fix memory $\mu$, original value map $f$, length $n$, band size $g$, owner $o$, and band record $r$. If row position $j$ stores value $f(\operatorname{start}(g,r.a)+j)$, owner $o$, and that original position in the three parallel arrays, those arrays satisfy the stored-incidence predicate for the row.

This representation lemma supplies the stored-array invariant for a newly emitted original-A band row.
explanation: Identify the row labels and verify the three stored-array components. This representation lemma supplies the stored-array invariant for a newly emitted original-A band row.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandRawA.Stored.keep_before_append
theorem_title: Appending disjoint incidence arrays preserves the stored prefix
natural_language_statement:
Let $\mu$ store a label list $L$ in three parallel arrays of common reserved capacity $C$, each ending before the next begins. Suppose an update to $\nu$ preserves cells outside the three append windows of length $m$, and $|L|+m\le C$. The original prefix $L$ remains stored in $\nu$.

This preservation lemma permits further owner rows to be appended without invalidating earlier physical incidences.
explanation: Capacity and separation place all prefix cells outside the append windows. This preservation lemma permits further owner rows to be appended without invalidating earlier physical incidences.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BandScales.bandDivisor_log_rate
theorem_title: Logarithmic rate of the band divisor
natural_language_statement:
As $n\to\infty$, the actual integer band divisor satisfies $$\frac{\log(\operatorname{bandDivisor}(n))}{\log n}\longrightarrow-\operatorname{bandShift}\,\varepsilon,$$ with the fixed schedule parameters shown.

This limit supplies the exact rounded divisor exponent when deriving the actual band-size and band-count rates.
explanation: Compute the limit from the rounded integer schedule. This limit supplies the exact rounded divisor exponent when deriving the actual band-size and band-count rates.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockSourceCatalogCosts.catalogCells_le_encoderCount
theorem_title: Catalog cells are bounded by the encoder count
natural_language_statement:
For input length $n$, let $J=\operatorname{blockCount}(\operatorname{inputBits}(n))$ and $\mu=\operatorname{mu}(n)$. Then $$\operatorname{catalogCells}(n)\le(J+464\mu+7)(232\mu+2)\operatorname{encoderCount}(n).$$

This estimate charges the complete retained catalog allocation to the finite encoder-count term of the ledger.
explanation: Bound the exact catalog layout by the finite encoder envelope. This estimate charges the complete retained catalog allocation to the finite encoder-count term of the ledger.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockSourceCoverInput.Input.of_kept
theorem_title: Retained cover input survives a protected-memory update
natural_language_statement:
Suppose $\mu$ stores cover input for size $h$ at its coefficient, candidate, and two histogram bases. If $\nu$ agrees below bound $b$, and every array ends by $b$ using its specified schedule and local-prime length, then the identical cover-input predicate holds in $\nu$.

This transport permits source construction to reuse protected coefficient and histogram tables after intervening calls.
explanation: Transport each defining read through protected-prefix agreement. This transport permits source construction to reuse protected coefficient and histogram tables after intervening calls.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.DenseGuardWanted.pair_indices_injective
theorem_title: Physical wanted-pair indices are injective
natural_language_statement:
Let wanted-setup output be stored in $\mu$ at base $f$, for source functions of lengths $N_L,N_R$, modulus $M$, and shift $d$. If valid slots $k,k'$ decode to the same left and right physical indices, then $k=k'$.

This injectivity prevents two physical wanted slots from being charged as the same original-index pair.
explanation: Recover the unique slot from its physical pair in the exact enumeration. This injectivity prevents two physical wanted slots from being charged as the same original-index pair.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.EncodedColorCoverData.source_controls
theorem_title: Reading retained cover source controls
natural_language_statement:
A stored cover-key output at base $f$, local size $h$, and block count $J$ returns at the designated offsets the local prime, bucket cap, width $464h$, schedule size, coefficient pointer, selected-candidate pointer, and both histogram pointers.

These header equations supply the concrete source controls read by the selected-color source-bank constructor.
explanation: Unpack the stored header and finite-input layout. These header equations supply the concrete source controls read by the selected-color source-bank constructor.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.EncodedColorParameterData.reads
theorem_title: Reading initialized integer parameters
natural_language_statement:
If the segment at parameter base $p$ contains initializer values for input length $n$, offsets $0,1,3,4,14,17,18$ contain respectively the bit count, micro-half size, block count, total block size, radix, band size, and prime-window size.

These read equations connect parameter-header RAM expressions to the exact integer schedule used in later contracts.
explanation: Evaluate the relevant initializer-list entries. These read equations connect parameter-header RAM expressions to the exact integer schedule used in later contracts.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.EncodedColorPipelineData.ordered
theorem_title: The encoded-color pipeline layout is ordered
natural_language_statement:
For free base $f$, input length $n$, and strictly increasing integer lists $A,B,C$, the prime metadata and initial header precede the cover base. The cover and four-cell wanted header precede the source controls. The three-cell controls and five-cell bank header fit before the pipeline finish address, using the exact list-dependent layout.

These address comparisons justify preservation of prime, cover, wanted, and source headers during subsequent allocation.
explanation: Compare layout formulas using nonnegativity of allocated extents. These address comparisons justify preservation of prime, cover, wanted, and source headers during subsequent allocation.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.EncodedColorPrimeData.Stored.of_kept
theorem_title: Retained prime metadata survives a protected-memory update
natural_language_statement:
Suppose $\mu$ stores the common-prime header, pool, and prefix moduli $q_i$ for base $f$, parameter $M$, and window $y$. If $\nu$ agrees below $b$ and the full prime allocation ends by $b$, the same stored-prime predicate holds in $\nu$.

This transport keeps the selected modulus and prime-chain metadata available while later pipeline regions are built.
explanation: Preserve every header, pool, and prefix-modulus read. This transport keeps the selected modulus and prime-chain metadata available while later pipeline regions are built.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalKeyEnumeration.rawOutput_abs_le
theorem_title: Absolute bound for a local raw output key
natural_language_statement:
For natural local size $h$, width $L$, local-field weight assignment $w$, and coordinate subset $Q\subseteq\{0,\ldots,L-1\}$, $$|\operatorname{rawOutput}(w,Q)|\le L\operatorname{localPrime}(h).$$

This bound places constructed local keys inside the finite word envelopes required by the actual key-building code.
explanation: Bound the coefficient sum by the coordinate count times the local prime. This bound places constructed local keys inside the finite word envelopes required by the actual key-building code.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.HierarchyScales.hierarchyEnvelope_log_rate
theorem_title: Logarithmic rate of the hierarchy envelope
natural_language_statement:
For any real constants $C,B$, $$\frac{\log(\operatorname{hierarchyEnvelope}(C,B,n))}{\log n}\longrightarrow\varepsilon C\quad(n\to\infty).$$ Here $\varepsilon$ is the fixed scale parameter.

This limit converts a hierarchy envelope into the polynomial exponent used by the final uniform runtime bound.
explanation: Combine the schedule limits in the defined envelope. This limit converts a hierarchy envelope into the polynomial exponent used by the final uniform runtime bound.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.Karatsuba.product_coeff_bound
theorem_title: A coefficient bound for polynomial multiplication
natural_language_statement:
Let integer lists $a,b$ have length at most $n$ and coefficient bound $U$. Every coefficient of their polynomial product satisfies $$|[X^j](A(X)B(X))|\le2nU^2\qquad(j\in\mathbb N).$$

This coefficient estimate supplies a safe word bound for the concrete Karatsuba product and its intermediate arrays.
explanation: Bound the finite convolution termwise. This coefficient estimate supplies a safe word bound for the concrete Karatsuba product and its intermediate arrays.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandLookup.search_meets
theorem_title: Binary band search returns the partition boundary
natural_language_statement:
A recursive search procedure reads a length-$n$ array $f$ at address $a$ and a width-$W$ power table. Suppose $f$ is partitioned for query $x$ at $K$, all declared address and word bounds hold, $L\le W$, and $k\le K<k+2^L$. If depth $d+L$ is allowed, the call on these controls returns $K$ within the declared search time and leaves memory unchanged.

This search contract supplies exact partition boundaries for physical band lookup without changing endpoint storage.
explanation: Induct on the remaining width and retain the interval invariant. This search contract supplies exact partition boundaries for physical band lookup without changing endpoint storage.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandPreprocessing.Represents.keep
theorem_title: Band representations survive protected-memory updates
natural_language_statement:
Let $g>0$ and a strictly increasing list $L$ represent an original list through stored values and endpoints in $\mu$. If $\mu'$ agrees below $b$ and the value and endpoint arrays fit below $b$, then the same representation holds in $\mu'$.

This transport lets later allocations retain the normalized values and exact band endpoints used by owner lookup.
explanation: Transfer all representation reads through memory agreement. This transport lets later allocations retain the normalized values and exact band endpoints used by owner lookup.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandRawAColor.tables_keep
theorem_title: Owner tables survive protected-memory updates
natural_language_statement:
Let band families $A,B,C$ have their enumeration tables stored at $t$ in $\mu$. If $\nu$ agrees below $b$ and the complete prescribed table extent ends by $b$, those tables remain stored in $\nu$.

This preservation fact keeps the computed owner tables valid during construction of physical original-A rows.
explanation: Preserve the entire table segment. This preservation fact keeps the computed owner tables valid during construction of physical original-A rows.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBandWeightedScoreSlice.meets
theorem_title: Computing a truncated band length
natural_language_statement:
Suppose procedure $p$ is the truncated-band-length body, $g>0$, $ig\le n$, and the word bound accommodates $n+g+4$. Its call on $(n,g,i)$ returns the exact truncated band length within the declared constant time and preserves memory.

This constant-time length query supplies the exact final truncated-band size to the weighted-score procedure.
explanation: Execute the straight-line arithmetic and minimum branch. This constant-time length query supplies the exact final truncated-band size to the weighted-score procedure.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightBruteThreeSum.poly_need
theorem_title: The finite fallback has polynomial resource needs
natural_language_statement:
The concrete brute-force 3SUM resource-need function satisfies the precise polynomial-need predicate of the light-language framework.

This polynomial-resource fact allows the finite fallback to participate in the same word-RAM compilation interface.
explanation: Bound its explicit space, word, and depth needs by fixed polynomials. This polynomial-resource fact allows the finite fallback to participate in the same word-RAM compilation interface.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightEncodedColorResult.meets
theorem_title: Materializing the encoded-color result header
natural_language_statement:
Suppose the prime, cover, wanted, control, and bank pointers precede output address $o$, eight output cells fit, the length and modulus fit words, and addresses fit words. The result-header procedure returns $o$ in at most 600 light steps, writes the specified eight-cell record, and preserves memory below $o$.

This record-writing contract exposes the completed selected-color pipeline through actual stored pointers and counts.
explanation: Execute the stores and check their safety and costs. This record-writing contract exposes the completed selected-color pipeline through actual stored pointers and counts.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightKaratsuba.joined_product
theorem_title: Karatsuba recombination recovers product coefficients
natural_language_statement:
Let integer lists $a,b$ have length $n=2h$. If three workspace blocks store the low-half product, high-half product, and product of half-sums, then for every $j$ the recombined value equals $$[X^j](A(X)B(X)).$$

This identity connects the stored three-product recombination to the polynomial coefficients required by cyclic correlation.
explanation: Reuses the platform-proved Karatsuba joining identity, with the identical coefficient-storage predicate. The platform checks that its complete proof type agrees with this existing target; no assumption or bound is added.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverMagnitude.rounds_bound
theorem_title: An exponential bound on the cover schedule
natural_language_statement:
For every natural local size $h$, $$\operatorname{scheduleSize}(h)\le2^{1029h+16}.$$

This explicit schedule bound contributes to the common local-cover magnitude and finite word-resource envelope.
explanation: Bound the exact finite schedule by the displayed power of two. This explicit schedule bound contributes to the common local-cover magnitude and finite word-resource envelope.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverMagnitude.cap_bound
theorem_title: An exponential bound on the local bucket cap
natural_language_statement:
For every natural local size $h$, $$\operatorname{localBucketCap}(h)\le2^{514h+6}.$$

This explicit cap bound controls the retained-bucket threshold inside the local-cover word and time estimates.
explanation: Use the finite estimates defining the selected local cap. This explicit cap bound controls the retained-bucket threshold inside the local-cover word and time estimates.

name: ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverResources.word_polynomial
theorem_title: A quadratic word envelope for local-cover setup
natural_language_statement:
If natural parameters $h,B$ satisfy the complete local-cover magnitude-bounds predicate, then $$\operatorname{setupWord}(h)\le2000B^2.$$

This quadratic estimate turns the common local-cover magnitude into a concrete setup word requirement.
explanation: Bound the setup word summands by the common envelope. This quadratic estimate turns the common local-cover magnitude into a concrete setup word requirement.
